cf.title: Fix recovery connection detail in EXEC_BACKEND builds

input.subject: [PATCH] Fix recovery connection detail in EXEC_BACKEND builds

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The problem is stated in message #1, the fix makes EXEC_BACKEND builds report the same DETAIL and HINT as fork() builds, and v2 reuses the existing CAC_state mechanism as Heikki Linnakangas suggested in message #2. Confidence is medium because the code was not read and nobody has replied to v2.

brief.title: Fix hot standby connection error detail in EXEC_BACKEND builds
brief.problem: In EXEC_BACKEND builds the backend does not inherit reachedConsistency from the postmaster. A connection rejected after consistency but before the hot standby snapshot is ready therefore gets the wrong DETAIL ("Consistent recovery state has not been yet reached") and no hint about transactions with more than 64 subtransactions. Users of EXEC_BACKEND builds, such as Windows, see the misleading message.
brief.proposed_design: v2 restores the CAC_NOTCONSISTENT code and has the postmaster pick it or CAC_NOTHOTSTANDBY before it launches the backend. The backend then chooses DETAIL and HINT from CAC_state alone. v1 instead passed reachedConsistency through BackendStartupData, and Heikki suggested the change to a separate CAC_* code.
user_visible_surface: Connection rejection DETAIL and HINT during hot standby startup change in EXEC_BACKEND builds to match fork() builds.
Internal enum CAC_state gains CAC_NOTCONSISTENT again (src/include/tcop/backend_startup.h).
author_claims: Only the reported DETAIL and HINT change; connection acceptance and recovery behavior do not.
Core regression tests pass on Linux in normal and EXEC_BACKEND builds.
Manual testing showed the expected DETAIL and HINT.
The author did not test on Windows.
brief.thread_state: Heikki Linnakangas reviewed v1 and suggested a new CAC_* code, and the author posted v2 that does this. Nobody has replied to v2 yet.
unclear: The material does not say whether the postmaster's view of consistency can be stale by the time the backend reports the error.
The thread does not say whether a test covers the new DETAIL or HINT, or whether a TAP test is possible.
The thread does not say which branches should get the fix.
The thread does not say when CAC_NOTCONSISTENT was removed, or why.

questions: Which branches should get the fix, and if back-patched, is CAC_NOTCONSISTENT added at the end of CAC_state so existing values keep their numbers?
Can the postmaster's view of consistency be out of date when it picks CAC_NOTCONSISTENT or CAC_NOTHOTSTANDBY, and does that differ from fork() builds today?
Does every remaining consumer of CAC_state handle the restored CAC_NOTCONSISTENT value?
Can a TAP test cover the DETAIL and HINT for a connection rejected after consistency but before the hot standby snapshot is ready?
Has anyone run v2 on Windows, the main platform that uses EXEC_BACKEND?

committability.owner_note: Heikki Linnakangas reviewed v1 in message #2 and suggested the design that v2 uses. Nobody has replied to v2 yet.
committability.liability: Small. The owner signs for one restored CAC_state value and the postmaster's choice between two rejection codes, plus the back-patch decision.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered the review in three days in message #3 and posted v2 as promised.

priority.reason: The fix affects only EXEC_BACKEND builds, such as Windows, during hot standby startup. The patch is about 4 KB across three files and removes the backend's reliance on an inherited postmaster variable.

provisional_note: Without the code, nobody checked whether all CAC_state consumers handle CAC_NOTCONSISTENT or where the postmaster reads the consistency state. The author did not test on Windows.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix cancelled queries when hot_standby_feedback = on
precedents_retrieved.summary: With hot_standby_feedback = on, standby queries still get cancelled when vacuum truncates a heap on the primary, because the AccessExclusiveLock taken for truncation is replayed on the standby. The final patch adds a new lock level, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE LOCAL, that vacuum uses for heap truncation and that is not WAL-logged, so standby queries must tolerate concurrent truncation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane showed that letting scans run during truncation leaves a race: concurrent scans can load to-be-truncated pages back into shared buffers before ftruncate, and reading past EOF on a standby can extend the relation. Alexander Korotkov agreed the patch had to be revised and sketched a new truncation design, but Robert Haas called it fragile and doubted it prevents stale buffers from being taken as valid. No new version followed, the existing patch failed initdb, and the entry was closed.
matched_queries: recovery snapshot not yet ready hot standby
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: If we ever have valid-looking buffers in shared_buffers after the corresponding data has been truncated away on disk, we've got to make sure that nobody ever confuses one of them with an actually-valid buffer.

precedents_retrieved.title: Replica sends an incorrect epoch in its hot standby feedback to the Master
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a bug in Postgres 9.6, 10 and 11 where a replica's nextXid can move backward during WAL replay in RecordKnownAssignedTransactionIds, so hot standby feedback carries a wrong epoch and the master ignores the replica's xmin. The one-line fix advances nextXid only when the new value is higher, as similar code elsewhere does.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The withdrawal was not a rejection of the fix. The author registered the patch in the commitfest more than once, and David Steele marked the duplicate entries 2462 and 2463 as withdrawn. The visible messages show no objection, and Thomas Munro agreed the nextXid assignment looked wrong.

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronous replay mode for avoiding stale reads on hot standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a synchronous_replay mode in which a commit on the primary waits until all available hot standbys have replayed it, and the primary grants time-limited leases to standbys. A standby without a valid lease rejects synchronous_replay transactions with a new error 40P02, so reads on standbys never miss a commit that has already returned on the primary.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last visible message, from February 2019, is a rebase by the author, and the entry was withdrawn in July 2019. Open items still visible at that point included missing TAP tests, an unexplained replication protocol corruption bug, and design questions from Masahiko Sawada about the GUCs.

precedents_retrieved.title: postgres_fdw - make cached connection functions tests meaningful with debug_invalidate_system_caches_always
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sets debug_invalidate_system_caches_always (later renamed debug_discard_caches) to off in the postgres_fdw regression tests, so that cache-clobbering builds stay stable. The tests for postgres_fdw_disconnect, postgres_fdw_disconnect_all and postgres_fdw_get_connections could then show the real function output instead of SELECT 1.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the patch assumes that turning debug_discard_caches off means no cache flushes, but flushes can still come at any time from sinval messages sent by other processes such as autovacuum. The tests would then pass most of the time but not always, which is not good enough for the buildfarm. The author agreed and marked the entry rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Not setting
debug_discard_caches doesn't mean that that can't happen, only that
you can't predict when it will happen.

precedents_retrieved.title: Close backend file handles on exec
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes BasicOpenFile open files with O_CLOEXEC, except in EXEC_BACKEND builds, so that programs a backend executes do not inherit its file descriptors. It came from a report of corruption on a server that uses pl/sh, where inherited descriptors were one suspected cause.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding to Peter Eisentraut's review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback about three weeks later. The review asked why EXEC_BACKEND was excluded, asked for an FD_CLOEXEC fallback on systems without O_CLOEXEC, a check of other places that open file descriptors, and a test that lists the descriptors an exec'd program inherits. It also noted that a code comment was wrong because archive_command and COPY to program call execve().
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Oskari, are you planning to answer to this review? As the thread has
died 3 weeks ago, I am marking this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql BACKEND_PID variable
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a built-in psql variable BACKEND_PID, set from PQbackendPID() at connect time and unset when the connection is lost. The stated benefits were tab completion of :BACKEND_PID, listing in \set, and no need to rerun pg_backend_pid() after a reconnect.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane and Peter Eisentraut held that the variable duplicates pg_backend_pid() and the %p prompt escape without making a real task easier. Tom Lane noted that while a slow query runs, the variable cannot be read any more than the function can be run. He also said each new built-in variable adds clutter. Andrew Dunstan moved the entry from Ready for Committer to Rejected, citing these comments, and the author agreed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't buy Pavel's argument that adding Yet Another built-in variable
adds ease of use.  I think what it mostly adds is clutter.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes in HOT handling of BRIN indexes
Reverted commit(s): Ignore BRIN indexes when checking for HOT udpates; Move test for BRIN HOT behavior to stats.sql
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 5753d4ee32 and fe60b67250 that modified HOT to
ignore BRIN indexes. The commit message for 5753d4ee32 claims that:

    When determining whether an index update may be skipped by using
    HOT, we can ignore attributes indexed only by BRIN indexes. There
    are no index pointers to individual tuples in BRIN, and the page
    range summary will be updated anyway as it relies on visibility
    info.

This is partially incorrect - it's true BRIN indexes don't point to
individual tuples, so HOT chains are not an issue, but the visibitlity
info is not sufficient to keep the index up to date. This can easily
result in corrupted indexes, as demonstrated in the hackers thread.

This does not mean relaxing the HOT restrictions for BRIN is a lost
cause, but it needs to handle the two aspects (allowing HOT chains and
updating the page range summaries) as separate. But that requires a
major changes, and it's too late for that in the current dev cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add function - pg_accept_connections_start_time()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a SQL function, renamed in v2 to pg_postmaster_open_time(), that returns the time the server last became ready to accept connections. Unlike pg_postmaster_start_time(), the value resets after crash recovery without a postmaster restart, so uptime and server restarts can be measured more accurately.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show an explicit rejection. The last message is Fujii Masao's review of v2, which asks the author to document that the timestamp changes when a standby is promoted. No reply or new patch version appears between that message on 2025-03-06 and the return on 2025-07-25. Tom Lane objected only to the side idea of extending postmaster.pid for pg_ctl status, not to the function itself.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert recent changes related to handling of 2PC files at recovery
precedents_retrieved.authors: Michael Paquier, Alexander Korotkov, Simon Riggs
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert recent changes related to handling of 2PC files at recovery
Reverted commit(s): Fix handling of orphaned 2PC files in the future at recovery; Fix failures with incorrect epoch handling for 2PC files at recovery; Make use FullTransactionId in 2PC filenames; Speedup 2PC recovery by skipping two phase state files in normal path
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit reverts 8f67f994e8ea (down to v13) and c3de0f9eed38 (down to
v17), as these are proving to not be completely correct regarding two
aspects:
- In v17 and newer branches, c3de0f9eed38's check for epoch handling is
incorrect, and does not correctly handle frozen epochs.  A logic closer
to widen_snapshot_xid() should be used.  The 2PC code should try to
integrate deeper with FullTransactionIds, 5a1dfde8334b being not enough.
- In v13 and newer branches, 8f67f994e8ea is a workaround for the real
issue, which is that we should not attempt CLOG lookups without reaching
consistency.  This exists since 728bd991c3c4, and this is reachable with
ProcessTwoPhaseBuffer() called by restoreTwoPhaseData() at the beginning
of recovery.

Per discussion with Noah Misch.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the corpus search returned no earlier attempt at the same or a similar idea. Message #1 points to a recent reachedConsistency discussion that mentioned this bug, and message #3 says CAC_NOTCONSISTENT existed before, but neither reports a rejection or revert reason that would apply here.

From the standards and compatibility angle there is nothing to object to. The patch adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump content or psql change. The only user-visible change makes the DETAIL and HINT in EXEC_BACKEND builds match what fork() builds already report. CAC_state is an internal enum, so restoring CAC_NOTCONSISTENT has no visible effect on clients. The thread does not say which branches get the fix. Clients that match on DETAIL text may see a different message after a minor upgrade, but that message is already the documented behaviour on other platforms.

The proposal has no persistent or cross-node state: no WAL record, on-disk format, catalog, protocol message or replication behavior changes. CAC_state is postmaster-to-backend startup data in the same build. If backpatched, appending the restored enum value avoids renumbering, but that is a detail for the committer and not a design objection.

The patch changes only which DETAIL and HINT a rejected connection gets during hot standby startup in EXEC_BACKEND builds. Fork() builds already show the same text to unauthenticated clients, so nothing new leaks, and the change touches no privilege, authentication or resource limit.

No maintenance or fit objection stands. This is a small bugfix that removes the backend's reliance on an inherited postmaster global; this pattern is a known source of EXEC_BACKEND bugs, so the change should lower future maintenance. The postmaster already computes CAC_state per connection, so non-users pay no per-connection or hot-path cost. Heikki Linnakangas, a committer who knows this area, shaped v2 in message #2. Not checked without the code: whether every remaining CAC_state consumer handles the restored CAC_NOTCONSISTENT value.

This is a bug fix for a wrong DETAIL and HINT in EXEC_BACKEND builds. No existing feature, setting or extension gives the correct message, so the need is not already met. The v2 design reuses the existing CAC_state mechanism. It does not add a second mechanism, so nothing from this angle applies.

This is a small bug fix: Windows and other EXEC_BACKEND builds report the wrong DETAIL and drop a HINT, so the message differs from fork() builds. A correctness fix for a misleading error message on a supported platform does not need a separate demand argument, and its cost is limited to one restored CAC_state code.
